target.name: Foundation Robotics
target.founder: Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi, Mike LeBlanc

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $50M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Foundation Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi, and Mike LeBlanc. The target has raised $50M+ to date and reportedly seeks $500M at a $3B+ valuation. The comp universe consists of 9 private robotics firms (including Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics at Series B and Seed stages) and 1 public comparable.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $50M total raised as a base proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $100M. Peer-median analysis draws on 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, with valuations of $1.8B (Bedrock), $1.6B (Dexterity), and $1.1B (Walden), producing a median implied value of $1.6B and a range of $1.1B–$1.8B.

Triangulation of these two methods supports a valuation range of $85M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $875M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate comparables and the gap between reported fundraising to date and the target's apparent Series B+ positioning. The peer-median method carries greater weight given the limited information on Foundation's own financials and the directness of like-stage robotics comparables. Key uncertainties include customer traction, manufacturing readiness, and whether the $3B+ ask reflects a materially more advanced stage than conventional Series A metrics would support.
